---
# Copy to NN-name.qmd (e.g. 01-cost-of-living.qmd). Files starting with "_" are not published.
title: "{Finding as one sentence: what changed, by how much, over when — include the data year, e.g. 2025}"
description: "{The question this study answers}"
number: "NN"
topic: "{Economy | Population | Social | Sectoral | International}"
data-period: "{Year(s) the data covers, e.g. 2025 or 2020–2025. Shown on cards and the page header}"
read-time: "{4}-minute read"
date: 2026-01-01
# Earlier studies this one connects to (optional; delete if none). They link back
# automatically. kind: follow-up (newer data or a deeper look at the same question),
# same-source, or same-topic. why: one line shown on BOTH pages, so name both studies
# by number and never say "here" or "this study".
related:
  - study: "{NN of an earlier study}"
    kind: "{follow-up | same-source | same-topic}"
    why: "{How the two connect, e.g. Both use Royal Brunei Police Force tables: X in NN, Y in NN.}"
---

```{python}
from shared.charts import highlight
from shared.components import (
    chart_card,
    method_and_sources,
    prev_next,
    related_studies,
    stat_tile,
    stat_tiles,
)
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

OUT = CASE_STUDIES / "{NN_name}" / "outputs"
df, provenance, notes = read_output(OUT / "{name}.csv")
```

::: {.study-intro}
{Introduction, 2–3 sentences: what this study looks at, which data and years, and its scope,
e.g. "It shows when and what changed, not why".}

It asks {one or two} questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **{Question 1?}**
:::

```{python}
# Layer 1: at most 3 tiles, each with a comparison.
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile("{Main measure}", "{+4.1%}", "{1.3 pts}", "vs {2024}", "up-bad"),
    stat_tile("{Comparison measure}", "{+1.3%}", "{0.4 pts}", "vs {2024}", "down-good"),
)
```

```{python}
# Layer 1: hero chart. One series in teal, the rest grey.
import plotly.express as px

fig = highlight(px.line(df, x="year", y="value", color="series"), focus="{series}")
chart_card(
    fig,
    title="{Chart takeaway: what to notice}",
    subtitle="{Measure, unit} · {2020–2025}",
    alt="{One-sentence summary of what the chart shows}",
    provenance=provenance,
    table=df,
)
```

## {What is examined, e.g. "Change by category, 2019 → 2025" (evidence, no verdict)}

{2–4 short paragraphs.}

## {Next thing examined}

{2–4 short paragraphs.}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
{Context the reader needs to read a number correctly, placed beside that number.}
:::

## Conclusion

- **{Question 1?}** {The answer, using the same numbers as the body.}

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
{Limitations in plain words: gaps, estimates, what the data can't show.}
:::

```{python}
# Earlier studies from `related:` and later ones that link here (nothing if none).
related_studies("{NN-name}.qmd", ROOT / "dashboard" / "case-studies")
```

```{python}
# Layer 4: method and sources, collapsed but always present.
method_and_sources(
    provenance,
    notes,
    steps=["{Download}", "{Cleaning and transformations}", "{Analysis}"],
    code_url=f"{REPO_URL}/tree/main/case_studies/{NN_name}",
)
```
